order: Build the alias layer and the roster kill switch before any rename. In `router/aliases.json`, declare every retired name's (role, rung) pair alongside the legacy identity it keeps while the old roster is installed, each with its ledger deprecation line. Have `resolveSeat()` evaluate the roster flag per order, 'legacy' returning the installed legacy agent unchanged and 'new' going through the casting tables and the degradation machine, with the declarative default at 'legacy' as the kill-switch home position, so rollback is a flag flip and no reload. Load the map under the same fail-closed discipline the other tables get: an unknown role, a rung the named role does not have, a missing legacy identity, or a bad roster default must each refuse construction. This is proven by old-name orders dispatching correctly under both flag values, flipped mid-session on one router instance, each emitting its deprecation line; and a tampered map fails the load closed.
claims: All items delivered. `router/aliases.json` declares all 16 retired names with their (role, rung) pair, legacy identity and deprecation line; `resolveSeat()` reads the roster flag per order and defaults to 'legacy', so rollback is a flag flip. Old-name orders dispatch correctly under both flags, flipped mid-session, each emitting its deprecation line. The map loads fail-closed on an unknown role, a rung the named role does not have, a missing legacy identity, or a bad default. For verification, section 12 hands `createRouter` a tampered map whose alias names a rung its role lacks and asserts the "does not have" refusal; 93 passed.
